1 │ # Post releases written without a dot, or without a number, are rejected
   2 │ 
   3 │ ## What happens now
   4 │ 
   5 │ If a version ends with a post release, the word post has to be written with a
   6 │ dot in front of it and a number after it. A version where the word post is
   7 │ joined straight onto the release numbers, or where it is preceded by a dash,
   8 │ or where no number follows the word, is turned down with an "Invalid version"
   9 │ error. The same restriction applies when the post release appears inside a
  10 │ requirement, so a rule that mentions such a post release is refused as well.
  11 │ 
  12 │ ## What should happen
  13 │ 
  14 │ Every spelling people actually use for a post release should be accepted: the
  15 │ word post attached to the numbers, the word post after a dot, the word post
  16 │ after a dash, the word in capitals, and the word with no number after it at
  17 │ all. When the number is left out, it should count as zero, and the version
  18 │ should be shown back in the standard form with the dot and the number filled
  19 │ in. Rules that mention a post release should accept the same spellings.
  20 │ 
  21 │ ## About this project
  22 │ 
  23 │ This project is a small library for working with version numbers. It reads a
  24 │ version that you give it, tells you whether the version is valid, sorts
  25 │ versions, and checks a version against a requirement such as a minimum or an
  26 │ exact match.
  27 │ 
  28 │ ## Problem this solves
  29 │ 
  30 │ A lot of projects name their post releases without a dot before the word post,
  31 │ with a dash instead, or with no number at all. Right now those real releases
  32 │ cannot be read at all, so a project that uses such a name cannot be installed,
  33 │ listed, or compared with others.
  34 │ 
  35 │ ## What changed
  36 │ 
  37 │ Post releases are read in all the usual spellings instead of only the one
  38 │ spelling with a dot and a number. A post release with no number is treated as
  39 │ having a number of zero, and it is printed back with the dot and the number
  40 │ added. Requirements that mention a post release accept the same spellings.
  41 │ How versions are ordered against each other, and every other part of a version
  42 │ such as the pre-release part, the development part and the local part, behave
  43 │ exactly as before. Nothing was taken away.
  44 │ 
  45 │ ## Impact
  46 │ 
  47 │ This is about compatibility and ease of use: version names that people
  48 │ already use stop being rejected, and nothing that worked before changes.
  49 │ 
  50 │ ## User experience
  51 │ 
  52 │ Before: I ask the library about a post release where the word post is joined
  53 │ straight to the numbers, or written after a dash, and I get an "Invalid
  54 │ version" error even though that name is used by a real project. After: the
  55 │ same name is accepted, and when I print the version back I get the standard
  56 │ form with the dot and, where the number was missing, a zero.
  57 │ 
  58 │ ## Hints
  59 │ 
  60 │ - /workspace/packaging/version.py
  61 │ - /workspace/tests/test_version.py
  62 │
